config.title: Build end to end test harness for core routes

intro.title: Build end to end test harness for core routes
intro.body: In this lesson, you will build an end-to-end test harness to verify that the core routes of your Node.js application work correctly from start to finish. You'll learn how to use the Supertest library to simulate HTTP requests and make assertions on the responses from your Express server. The main technologies involved are Node.js, the Express framework, and the Mocha test runner with Chai for assertions. By the end, you'll have a set of automated tests that check your routes return the expected status codes and data, helping you catch bugs early.
intro.usecase: End-to-end test harnesses are essential for validating critical user workflows in production applications. For example, e-commerce platforms use them to test the complete checkout flow—from adding items to cart through payment processing and order confirmation. Financial dashboards rely on these tests to ensure data visualization and transaction reporting work correctly across all integrated services. API-driven applications test authentication flows and data persistence to prevent regressions in user-facing functionality.

objectives: Initialize a test environment for Node.js routes using a testing framework
Configure test suites to validate core route endpoints
Implement test cases that simulate HTTP requests to route handlers
Construct assertions to verify route response status codes and data structures
Integrate route dependencies and middleware into the test harness
Manipulate test data to validate route behavior under different conditions
Control test execution order and environment setup for end-to-end testing

steps.title: Import required testing modules (supertest, jest, express)
steps.instruction: At the top of your test file, import the supertest, jest, and express modules.
steps.hint: Use require() statements to import the modules. You'll need supertest for making HTTP requests, jest for the testing framework, and express for your app.
steps.seedCode: // Import supertest, jest, and express modules here
steps.expectedOutcome: The test file will have the necessary testing modules imported at the top.
successCriteria: supertest, jest, and express are imported using require() statements.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've imported some modules, but you're missing one or more. Make sure to import supertest, jest, and express.
steps.feedbackWrong: The imports aren't correct. You need to import supertest, jest, and express modules using require() statements.

steps.title: Import the app module to test
steps.instruction: Import the Express app instance from your main application file. Assume the app is exported from './app.js'.
steps.hint: Use a require statement to import the app module from the correct path.
steps.analogousExample:
// Importing a module in Node.js
const myModule = require('./myModule');
steps.expectedOutcome: The app instance is imported and available for testing.
successCriteria: The app instance is imported from './app.js'.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure you're importing from './app.js' and assigning it to a variable.
steps.feedbackWrong: Check the import path and syntax. You need to import the app from './app.js'.

steps.title: Initialize test suite with describe block
steps.instruction: Create a describe block to group all route tests together. Use the test description 'Core Routes'.
steps.hint: Use the describe function from Jest to create a test suite. It takes a description string and a callback function containing your tests.
steps.expectedOutcome: A describe block is added to organize your route tests under the 'Core Routes' description.
successCriteria: The code contains a describe block with 'Core Routes' as the description string and an empty callback function.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure you have a complete describe block with both the description string and callback function.
steps.feedbackWrong: The describe block isn't quite right. Remember to use describe('Core Routes', () => {}) to create your test suite structure.

steps.title: Create test for GET /health route
steps.instruction: Inside the describe block, write a test case that makes a GET request to the /health endpoint using supertest.
steps.hint: Use the test() or it() function from Jest to define the test case. The first argument is a description string, and the second is an async callback function that makes the request and asserts the response.
steps.expectedOutcome: A test case is added inside the describe block that sends a GET request to /health and checks the response.
successCriteria: The test case uses test() or it(), makes a GET request to /health with supertest, and includes at least one assertion (e.g., checking status code).
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've started the test case, but it might be missing the request, assertion, or async handling. Ensure you use supertest to make the GET request and check the response.
steps.feedbackWrong: The test case for GET /health is not correctly implemented. Review the example and ensure you're using supertest within an async test function.

steps.title: Add assertions for health route response
steps.instruction: Inside the test for GET /health, add assertions to check that the response status is 200 and the response body contains a 'status' property equal to 'ok'.
steps.hint: Use the response object from supertest to call .expect() for status code and body property.
steps.analogousExample:
// Example: asserting response status and body
response.expect(200).expect({ status: 'ok' });
steps.expectedOutcome: The test will validate that the /health route returns the correct HTTP status and response structure.
successCriteria: The test includes assertions for status code 200 and a response body with status: 'ok'.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track. Make sure to check both the status code and the response body property.
steps.feedbackWrong: The test is missing assertions for the response. Add .expect() calls to check status and body.

steps.title: Create test for POST /api/data route
steps.instruction: Add a new test case inside the describe block that makes a POST request to '/api/data' with a sample request body.
steps.hint: Use the same pattern as the GET /health test, but change the method to .post() and include a .send() call with JSON data.
steps.expectedOutcome: A new test case for POST /api/data is added to the test suite with a sample request body.
successCriteria: The test case uses .post() method, targets '/api/data' endpoint, and includes .send() with JSON data.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've added a test case, but check if it uses .post() and includes a .send() with JSON data.
steps.feedbackWrong: The test case is missing or doesn't match the required structure for POST /api/data.

steps.title: Add assertions for POST route response
steps.instruction: Inside the POST /api/data test case, add assertions to check that the response status code is 201 and the response body contains a success message.
steps.hint: Use the response object from supertest to assert the status code and body properties. Remember to use async/await with the test.
steps.expectedOutcome: The POST route test will validate that the API returns the correct status code and response body structure.
successCriteria: The test includes assertions for response.status and response.body properties.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've added some assertions, but make sure to check both the status code and response body.
steps.feedbackWrong: The test doesn't include the required assertions. Review the example and try again.

steps.title: Create test for 404 route handling
steps.instruction: Inside the existing describe block, add a new test case that makes a GET request to a non-existent route like '/nonexistent'.
steps.hint: Add another 'it' block after your POST test. Use supertest(app).get() with a route that doesn't exist in your app.
steps.expectedOutcome: A new test case is added to verify your app returns a 404 status for routes that don't exist.
successCriteria: The describe block contains a third 'it' test case that makes a GET request to '/nonexistent' (or similar non-existent route).
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've added a test case, but make sure it's making a request to a route that doesn't exist in your app (like '/nonexistent').
steps.feedbackWrong: The test case for 404 handling is missing or incorrect. Add an 'it' block that makes a GET request to a non-existent route.

steps.title: Add assertions for 404 response
steps.instruction: Inside the 404 route test case, add assertions to check that a request to a non-existent route returns a 404 status code and an appropriate error message in the response body.
steps.hint: Use the supertest request to make a GET request to a route that doesn't exist (like '/nonexistent'), then chain .expect() assertions for status code and response body.
steps.expectedOutcome: The test case will validate that your app correctly handles unknown routes by returning a 404 status and an error message.
successCriteria: The 404 test case includes assertions for both status code (404) and response body containing an error message.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've added some assertions, but make sure to check both the status code and the response body content.
steps.feedbackWrong: The test case doesn't include the required assertions. Review the example and try again.

steps.title: Run the test suite
steps.instruction: Execute your test suite by running the npm test command in your terminal.
steps.hint: Make sure you're in your project directory and have the test script configured in package.json.
steps.analogousExample:
// Similar: running tests for another module
npm test
steps.expectedOutcome: All three tests should pass, confirming your test harness works correctly.
successCriteria: The test suite runs without errors and shows all tests passing.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: Some tests may have failed. Check your assertions and route implementations.
steps.feedbackWrong: The test suite didn't run. Ensure you're in the correct directory and have the test script configured.
